context.//: Deployment settings. The Google client id is not a secret (the secret itself lives in Secrets Manager under googleSecretName); keeping it here rather than passing -c on every deploy means the second, siteUrl pass can't accidentally drop the Google provider by omitting it.
context.//siteUrl: The origin the site used before statcastsicko.com. It still serves the app, so it stays a Cognito callback — pinned here because the distribution's own domain can't be read back into the user pool client without recreating the dependency cycle.
context.// authDomain: Cognito serves sign-in from auth.statcastsicko.com rather than the amazoncognito.com prefix domain, a candidate remedy for the iOS-only Google sign-in failure (cause inferred, not proven - see SickoStackProps.authDomainName). Pinned here rather than passed with -c so a deploy that forgets the flags cannot silently revert the cutover. TO ROLL BACK: set authDomainLive to false and deploy - sign-in returns to the prefix domain, which is never removed and never stopped serving; then invalidate CloudFront so config.json refreshes at the edge. Removing authDomainName as well tears down the cert, the domain and its DNS records. Both redirect URIs must stay on the Google OAuth client while either host can serve a sign-in.
